slides.text: People think the thick grey fog rolling through the cobblestone streets of London is just weather. They don’t see the jagged teeth hidden in the mist, or the shadowy claws scraping against the streetlamps. They are Nightmares, born from the city's collective sleeping dread. I am a Sweeper. Armed with a broom of enchanted ash-wood and a lantern of trapped starlight, I work the graveyard shift to keep the mortal world entirely safe from its own sleeping mind.

It’s a lonely, thankless job. If we fail, the fog breaches the windows, and humanity wakes up with hollow, screaming eyes. Last Tuesday, the mist thickened into something unprecedented. A towering, serpentine beast of pure terror materialized over the Thames. My lantern sputtered, the starlight dimming against its crushing aura. It was an ancient fear, older than the city itself. I gripped my broom, my knees trembling, knowing I was completely alone and entirely outmatched.

The beast lunged, its jaw opening to swallow me whole. Suddenly, a dozen golden lanterns flared in the darkness behind me. I turned to see the daytime Sweepers, the midnight couriers, and even the stone gargoyles of the cathedral, all stepping through shimmering portals. 'You didn't think you had to clean this mess alone, did you?' grinned an old witch, tossing me a vial of pure dawn. Together, we raised our lights and swept the darkness away.
